title: Introduction & Salutations
content:
Om Sai Ram.

This is Chapter 1 of the Shri Sai Satcharita.

Blessed is the country of Shirdi, blessed is its soil where the great saint Sai Baba lived. This chapter introduces the Satcharita, the sacred biography of Shri Sai Baba of Shirdi written by Hemadpant (Govind Raghunath Dabholkar).

The author first salutes Sri Ganesha, Saraswati, the Guru, and all saints. He then explains why he undertook the writing of this work — to spread the teachings and leelas of Sai Baba for the benefit of devotees.

Sai Baba's life was his message. His teaching was through experience and example. He showed that the path to God is through devotion (bhakti), faith (shraddha), and patience (saburi).

title: The Advent of Sai Baba in Shirdi
content:
Om Sai Ram.

This is Chapter 2 of the Shri Sai Satcharita.

This chapter describes the first appearance of Sai Baba in Shirdi. He appeared as a young lad of sixteen, sitting under a neem tree in deep meditation. The villagers were astonished to see this young boy practicing such hard penance.

No one knew his name, parentage, or birthplace. He seemed indifferent to all worldly things. Mhalsapati, a devotee, was the first to call him 'Sai' — meaning saint or holy one.

Baba stayed in Shirdi for the rest of his life, turning it into a place of pilgrimage for millions of devotees.

title: The Greatness of the Guru
content:
Om Sai Ram.

This is Chapter 3 of the Shri Sai Satcharita.

This chapter emphasizes the importance of the Guru in spiritual life. Sai Baba taught that without the grace of a Sadguru, spiritual progress is impossible.

The Guru removes the darkness of ignorance and lights the lamp of knowledge. Baba himself was such a Sadguru — he guided his devotees on the path of self-realization through his own unique methods.

Baba said: 'I give people what they want in the hope that they will begin to want what I want to give them.'

title: Hemadpant's Resolve to Write
content:
Om Sai Ram.

This is Chapter 4 of the Shri Sai Satcharita.

This chapter narrates how Hemadpant was inspired to write the Satcharita. Initially hesitant about his ability to write about Sai Baba's infinite greatness, he received Baba's assurance and blessing to proceed.

Baba said to him: 'I myself will write my own story through you. Simply sit in a place, I shall inspire you from within.'

With this divine assurance, Hemadpant began the sacred work that would become one of the most beloved spiritual texts in India.

title: Sai Baba's Daily Life
content:
Om Sai Ram.

This is Chapter 5 of the Shri Sai Satcharita.

This chapter describes the daily routine of Sai Baba in Shirdi. Baba lived in a dilapidated mosque which he called 'Dwarkamai' — the mother of compassion.

He kept a sacred fire (dhuni) always burning, which represented the burning away of worldly desires. He would go for bhiksha (alms) to a few houses in the village, mixing all the food together and sharing it with animals, birds, and devotees.

His life was one of simplicity, compassion, and complete detachment from material possessions.

title: Baba's Teachings on Faith and Patience
content:
Om Sai Ram.

This is Chapter 6 of the Shri Sai Satcharita.

This chapter elaborates on Baba's two cardinal principles: Shraddha (faith) and Saburi (patience). Baba taught that these two virtues are the foundation of all spiritual progress.

Shraddha means complete faith in the Guru and God, without doubt or wavering. Saburi means patience and perseverance — continuing on the spiritual path regardless of obstacles.

Baba said: 'If you develop faith and devotion, you will surely attain self-realization.'

title: Baba's Miracles and Leelas
content:
Om Sai Ram.

This is Chapter 7 of the Shri Sai Satcharita.

This chapter recounts some of the miraculous events in Baba's life. Though Baba appeared to be an ordinary fakir, he demonstrated supernatural powers time and again — not to impress, but to strengthen the faith of devotees.

From lighting lamps with water, to curing incurable diseases, to being present at multiple places simultaneously — Baba's leelas were beyond human comprehension.

Yet Baba always attributed everything to the Almighty, saying he was merely a servant of God.

title: Devotees' Experiences - Part 1
content:
Om Sai Ram.

This is Chapter 8 of the Shri Sai Satcharita.

This chapter narrates the experiences of various devotees who came to Shirdi seeking Baba's blessings. Each devotee had unique problems — health, family, finances — and Baba helped each one according to their needs.

Baba treated all equally — Hindu or Muslim, rich or poor, learned or illiterate. His message was universal: 'All are one. God is the inner ruler of all.'

Baba's grace worked in mysterious ways — sometimes through a direct word of advice, sometimes through a symbolic action, and sometimes through dreams and visions.

title: Baba's Way of Teaching
content:
Om Sai Ram.

This is Chapter 10 of the Shri Sai Satcharita.

This chapter explains Baba's unique teaching methods. Unlike traditional teachers, Baba taught through stories, parables, and experiences rather than formal discourses.

He would tell seemingly simple stories that contained deep spiritual truths. Each devotee would understand the story according to their own level of spiritual development.

Baba said: 'I do not teach with words alone. I give what is needed at the right time.'

title: Epilogue - Baba Lives Forever
content:
Om Sai Ram.

This is Chapter 53 (final) of the Shri Sai Satcharita.

Baba assured his devotees: 'I shall be active and vigorous even from the tomb. My mortal remains will speak from the tomb. My bones will give you assurance.'

Sai Baba's teachings continue to guide millions of devotees worldwide. His message of love, faith, and patience remains as relevant today as it was a century ago.

Om Sai Ram.
